topic.angle: From slave revolt to a new state, and the price of recognition

card.title: The revolt that built a country

panels.text: In August 1791, enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue rose against colonial rule. The fight would last until 1 January 1804.
Toussaint Louverture, a self-educated former domestic slave, became one of its most successful commanders. He decided to fight for France if it would agree to free all the slaves.
The result was rare. Few slave rebellions in history led to a new state that was free from slavery and ruled by formerly enslaved people. This one created Haiti.
The twist: France did not recognise Haiti's independence until 1825, and only if Haiti agreed to pay an indemnity of 150 million francs.
